items.title: p-e-w/heretic
items.summary: Training-free language model modification: Remove censorship, suppress slop, reduce sycophancy, and more https://heretic-project.org Heretic Training-free language model modification Remove censorship, suppress slop, reduce sycophancy, and more. All in an afternoon, on your gaming PC. Modify any LLM that you can run on your hardware[1] Heretic is a unique tool that lets you do what only corporations with access to massive computing power usually do: Modify, rather than merely run, language models. It does not perform expensive training; rather, it uses a collection of mathematical techniques to steer behavior based on contrasting example prompts and matching scorers. Heretic can, depending on the configuration: Suppress refusals/remove censorship (this is the default action) Reduce slop (config.noslop.toml) Reduce humor (config.nohumor.toml) Reduce sycophancy (config.nosyco.toml) Alter emotional alignment (config.emotions.toml) Shorten response length (config.terse.toml) and many, many other things. ‼️ Using Heretic does NOT require understanding how language models work internally ‼️ In fact, you can go from zero to removing censorship from your first model in a matter of seconds. Heretic supports most dense models, including many multimodal models, several different MoE architectures, and many modern hybrid models. The community has created and published thousands of models with Heretic. Heretic models have been independently benchmarked using standard metrics like MMLU and GSM8K, and have been found to compare favorably against models produced with competing abliteration tools.[2][3] Usage Prepare a Python 3.10+ environment with PyTorch 2.6+ installed as appropriate for your hardware. Then run: pip install -U heretic-llm heretic Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 Replace Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 with whatever model you want to process. By default, Heretic performs censorship removal (refusal suppression). If you want to do something else, choose one of the configuration files linked above, or write your own. See config.default.toml for available configuration options. Heretic loads the configuration from config.toml in the working directory by default, or from the file path in the HERETIC_CONFIG_FILE environment variable. Important Configuration files made for Heretic 1.x are not compatible with Heretic 2.x! See the migration guide for what you need to change in order to make your old configurations work. At the start of a program run, Heretic benchmarks the system to determine the optimal batch size to make the most of the available hardware. On an RTX 3090, with the default configuration, processing Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 takes about 30-40 minutes. After Heretic has finished processing a model, you are given the choice to save the model, upload it to Hugging Face, chat with it to test how well it works, run standard benchmarks on it, or any combination of those actions. Controlling what Heretic does using scorer plugins Heretic steers model behavior by optimizing one or multiple scores. Scores are computed by scorer plugins. You can easily write your own scorers to get full control over what Heretic does to models. The Scorer interface (abstract base class) your scorer needs to inherit from is defined in scorer.py. The only required method is get_score, but there is more machinery (such as settings management) available when you need it. By default, Heretic scores models by refusal rate (implemented in keyword_rate.py) and KL divergence (implemented in kl_divergence.py). Additional scorers are available in the scorers directory. These scorers can serve as examples for your own implementations, and can easily be adapted to your needs. Scorers are configured through the main configuration file. Which scorer plugins are active is determined by the scorers setting, which also controls whether a scorer's score should be minimized or maximized during optimization. Any number of scorers can be used simultaneously, and their scores will be co-optimized. Multiple instances of the same scorer can be configured with different settings. See the configuration file for the full documentation of this mechanism. The path to a scorer plugin can be specified either as a fully qualified import path (fully.qualified.module.MyScorerClass) or as a file path followed by a class name (path/to/plugin.py:MyScorerClass). You do not have to modify the Heretic package code in order to use your own plugins. Heretic also has modifier plugins, which are described in the next section. How Heretic works Heretic combines a pluggable modifier (interface in modifier.py) with a TPE-based hyperparameter optimizer powered by Optuna. The optimizer finds a set of parameters that, when passed to the modifier, minimize or maximize a set of configurable scores on the resulting model (see above). Heretic ships with two modifiers: Arbitrary-Rank Ablation (ARA)[4]: This is the default modifier, and was specifically developed for use in Heretic. You can find an overview of how ARA works in the original pull request, and see the precise implementation in ara.py. Directional ablation aka "abliteration"[5]: The classic method for refusal suppression. Heretic's implementation uses a flexible ablation weight kernel over the layers, and supports both projected abliteration[6] and norm preservation (MPOA)[7]. The complete code is in abliteration.py. You can use the modifiers setting to switch between modifier implementations. Despite the name of the setting using a plural form, Heretic currently allows only a single modifier for a given processing run. This may change in the future. Reproducibility and the Heretic Grimoire Heretic has the ability to create reproducible models whose repositories contain all information required to produce a byte-for-byte identical model on demand, provided that the environment is perfectly identical to the original one. PyTorch doesn't guarantee that operations return identical outputs unless hardware, drivers, operating system, and the entire software stack including all package versions are exactly the same. Heretic manages all that complexity for you. When uploading a processed model to Hugging Face, Heretic offers to include reproducibility information. This is entirely optional, but if you choose to do so, the uploaded repository will contain a reproduce folder with detailed instructions for recreating the model (example). This folder contains both human-readable instructions and a machine-readable manifest file named reproduce.json, which includes all the information Heretic needs to automatically reproduce the model. Automatic reproduction can be performed with heretic --reproduce path/to/reproduce.json Heretic will guide you through the process, checking your environment against the one that was used to create the model, and pointing out potentially problematic mismatches. The multi-hour computations that were required to make the original model do not have to be re-done, and the entire process typically takes a few minutes. After you have exported the resulting model, Heretic will verify the hashes of the weight files against those stored in the reproduction manifest (they may or may not be identical, depending on how closely your system resembles the original one). Many people have uploaded models with reproducibility information to Hugging Face. Since a reproduction manifest is only around 9 kilobytes in size, these manifests form a portable library of models that can be reproduced at will. That library is called the Heretic Grimoire. You can view it here. But you don't have to rely on an externally hosted web application to access the library of manifests: The Grimoire is fundamentally designed as a distributed system, and you can fetch your own local copies of publicly available manifests from Hugging Face whenever you want by running heretic --collect-reproducibles path/to/target/folder/ You now have a local backup of all reproducible Heretic models, properly catalogued. To update this collection, simply run the command again. It functions as an append-only backup, never deleting files even if the corresponding model no longer exists on Hugging Face. Heretic is made by humans! Unlike lots of AI-related software today (and indeed lots of software in general), Heretic is not "vibe-coded". All of my commits to this project until November 2026 were written 100% by hand, the way I have been doing programming for decades. I have been using LLM assistance very sparingly since. While many Heretic contributors use coding agents, I carefully review every single line of code that I merge. There's no "LGTM" here! Don't believe me? Check out this pull request, which accumulated almost 350 human-written comments over more than 7 months as we discussed the implementation. And here is another PR with more than 200 comments. I am the opposite of a luddite and I have used agents liberally for other projects, but I am proud of the code I write and so far can't quite bring myself to let a machine write it for me in a project I care so much about. As a result, Heretic has a lean, relatively simple codebase that in my opinion, and in that of some others, is a pleasure to work on. If you like that, join us! Hop on the Discord and tell us about your ideas for improvements, or directly file an issue or open a PR. Prior art I'm aware of the following implementations of abliteration techniques that were publicly available when Heretic was first released (November 2025): AutoAbliteration abliterator.py wassname's Abliterator ErisForge Removing refusals with HF Transformers deccp Note that Heretic was written from scratch, and does not reuse code from any of those projects. Acknowledgments The development of Heretic was informed by: The original abliteration paper (Arditi et al. 2024) Maxime Labonne's article on abliteration, as well as some details from the model cards of his own abliterated models, such as the use of non-constant ablation weights Jim Lai's articles describing "projected abliteration" and "norm-preserving biprojected abliteration" Thousands of interactions with members of the community Citation If you use Heretic for your research, please cite it using the following BibTeX entry: @misc{heretic, author = {Weidmann, Philipp Emanuel}, title = {Heretic: Training-free language model modification}, year = {2025}, publisher = {GitHub}, journal = {GitHub repository}, howpublished = {\url{https://github.com/p-e-w/heretic}} } License Copyright © 2025-2026 Philipp Emanuel Weidmann (pew@worldwidemann.com) + contributors This program is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify it under the terms of the GNU Affero General Public License as published by the Free Software Foundation, either version 3 of the License, or (at your option) any later version. This program is distributed in the hope that it will be useful, but WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY; without even the implied warranty of MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE. See the GNU Affero General Public License for more details. You should have received a copy of the GNU Affero General Public License along with this program. If not, see https://www.gnu.org/licenses/. By contributing to this project, you agree to release your contributions under the same license. Heretic supports on-the-fly 4-bit model quantization with bitsandbytes, which can reduce the amount of VRAM required to process a model to the same amount that is used to run a typical quantized version of it, at a slight accuracy cost. Set the quantization option to bnb_4bit to enable this. ↩︎ Qwen2.5-7B: Three-Way Abliteration Comparison: "Heretic is the most surgical and most effective." ↩︎ Gemma 4 E4B: 23 Abliteration Variants Compared: "Best overall: heretic." ↩︎ Weidmann 2026. A preprint explaining the technique will be available soon. ↩︎ Arditi et al. 2024 ↩︎ Lai 2025 (1) ↩︎ Lai 2025 (2) ↩︎

items.title: phone-harness/phone-harness
items.summary: let your agent control your phone https://phone-harness.com Enable Claude Code, Codex, or any agent to use your real phone. The agent can scroll, tap, type, and read your phone with no jailbreak, no Xcode, and nothing installed on the phone. iPhone through the Mac's iPhone Mirroring window Android over adb from macOS, Linux or Windows Phone Harness Cloud phone: an Android over adb, or an iPhone over HTTPS ● agent: wants to open Weather │ ● find_text("Weather") → (400, 468) │ ● tap(400, 468) → reads the screen → forecast is up ✓ done Try Phone Harness Cloud → Hosted iPhones and Androids with stealth, real numbers, 2FA, and unlimited devices Get started by sending the setup prompt to your coding agent. Demo Task: "Buy me a Waymo to Delah Coffee from my current location." Setup For the CLI, send this setup prompt to your agent (Claude Code, Codex, Grok Bot, and more): Install or upgrade phone-harness to the latest stable version with uv using Python 3.12, register the skill from `phone-harness skill`, then read https://github.com/phone-harness/phone-harness/blob/main/onboarding.md and walk me through it. Follow https://github.com/phone-harness/phone-harness/blob/main/install.md if setup or connection fails. The agent installs the CLI, asks which phone to use, and walks you through the steps that need your hands. What each phone needs: Phone Needs iPhone macOS 15+, iPhone Mirroring paired to an iOS 18+ iPhone, Accessibility and Screen Recording permission Android adb and USB debugging, on macOS, Linux or Windows Cloud Android / iPhone Phone Harness Cloud account; cloud Android also needs adb phone-harness doctor checks the setup. Full details: install.md and setup/. MCP: add https://mcp.phone-harness.com/mcp to any MCP client (setup). Cloud Android and iPhone only for now. Hermes Agent: hermes plugins install phone-harness/phone-harness/integrations/hermes. See integrations/hermes. OpenClaw: openclaw plugins install clawhub:phone-harness. See integrations/openclaw. Usage phone-harness <<'PY' open_app("Notes") tap_text("New Note") type_text("hello from the harness") print([o["text"] for o in screen()][:10]) PY Helpers are pre-imported; helpers.py has the full list. The agent saves its own helpers in ~/.phone-harness/agent-workspace. Phone Harness Cloud No phone on your desk, or need more than one? Phone Harness Cloud hosts them for you: Android phones on demand: a fresh one per session, or a saved phone that keeps its apps and logins. Dedicated real iPhones, driven over HTTPS from any OS. A live view of the phone in your browser while the agent works. phone-harness cloud login # once: approve in your browser phone-harness cloud ls # phones on the account, and any live session phone-harness cloud start # cloud.phone if set, else a temporary Android; 15 min (--for 90s, 15m) phone-harness cloud start ios # the account's iPhone, when only one is listed phone-harness <<'PY' print(screenshot()) PY phone-harness cloud stop # ends the session; a saved Android is written back The same helpers drive a cloud phone: an Android over adb, an iPhone over HTTPS. cloud start takes a phone's name or id from cloud ls, or ios / android; with none it starts a temporary Android. phone-harness cloud lists every command. No cloud iPhone on the account yet, or need more of them? Reserve them with a $20 per phone refundable deposit. The command prints a quote, which is the authoritative figure, and a Stripe Checkout link. You pay in your browser, and that payment is what holds your place in the queue, which is in the order deposits were paid; the CLI never pays for you. phone-harness cloud reserve --type iphone --plan monthly --qty 2 \ --use-case "Testing our app on real iPhones" --open phone-harness cloud reservations # status, place in the queue, deposit, when it was paid phone-harness cloud reservations cancel ID # leave the queue; the deposit still held goes back to the card that paid --type is iphone or iphone-esim, and --plan is monthly or annual. Reservations are for iPhones only (with or without eSIM). Cloud Android emulators are on the $20 plan and are not reserved. The plan starts when a phone is handed over; the deposit comes off its first bill and is then no longer refundable. An account can have five unpaid reservations an hour, and cancelling one does not free a place. How it works Every phone sits behind the same helpers, so a script written for one runs on the others. iPhone: captures the iPhone Mirroring window, reads it with Apple's Vision OCR, and sends taps, swipes and typing as input events. Android: adb for screenshots and input, the accessibility tree for text. USB or Wi-Fi. Cloud Android: the same as Android, over adb to a hosted phone. Cloud iPhone: ops over HTTPS. phone-harness config set platform ios|android picks the default phone. phone-harness update upgrades the CLI, and it prints one line when a new version is out (PHONE_HARNESS_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1 silences it). Limits Unlocking the iPhone pauses mirroring; a PIN-locked Android needs the user. OCR sees text, not icons. Unlabeled controls need a screenshot and a vision-capable model. No multi-touch, no camera or Face ID flows. DRM video renders black. Connecting the phone is always the user's job. Sponsor phone-harness is free and maintained in my own time. Sponsoring keeps it that way.

items.title: pytorch/torchtitan
items.summary: A PyTorch native platform for training generative AI models A PyTorch-native platform for pretraining and post-training generative AI models at scale Quick start · Models · Features · RL · Docs · Contributing torchtitan is a clean-room, PyTorch-native implementation of large-scale training. One readable codebase takes a model from pretraining through supervised fine-tuning to reinforcement learning, composing FSDP, tensor, pipeline, context, and expert parallelism without rewriting the model. Composable parallelism. Models declare how they shard; FSDP2, TP, PP, CP, and EP stack into N-D layouts through DeviceMesh and DTensor. Built for research. Minimal, hackable code; every run is a Python recipe you can read, copy, and modify. Pretraining to RL in one stack. TitanRL runs the same model definitions and kernels in the trainer and in vLLM generation, with a bitwise-reproducible batch-invariant mode. Frontier models and techniques. DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, gpt-oss, Llama, and FLUX, with MXFP8/NVFP4 low precision, Dist-MoE, CUDA graphs, and more. Note torchtitan is under active development. To use the latest features, use a recent PyTorch nightly. Latest news [2026/10] Zephon, a data loader by DatologyAI, released its TorchTitan integration. Zephon keeps the same training batches in the same order even when your GPU count changes (elastic determinism). Check out the blog post on pytorch.org. [2026/08] TitanRL is a hackable RL stack for scaling and debugging. It reuses TorchTitan model definitions and kernels across training and vLLM generation and supports batch-invariant mode. [2025/11] AMD released an optimized fork of torchtitan for AMD GPUs. [2025/10] We released torchtitan v0.2.0. [2025/10] SkyPilot now supports torchtitan! See the tutorial. Older news [2025/07] We published instructions on how to add a model to torchtitan. [2025/04] Our paper was accepted by ICLR 2025. [2024/12] GPU MODE lecture on torchtitan. [2024/07] Presentation at PyTorch Conference 2024. Quick start 1. Install with a PyTorch nightly (Python 3.11+). Replace cu132 with your CUDA or ROCm build. git clone https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan && cd torchtitan pip install --pre torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/nightly/cu132 pip install -r requirements.txt 2. Train a debug model. It uses the tokenizer bundled with the tests, so no download is needed. NGPU=1 ./run_train.sh # Llama 3 debug model, 10 steps 3. Train a real model. Download the tokenizer (Llama weights require access on Hugging Face), then select a recipe by module and function name: python scripts/download_hf_assets.py --repo_id meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B --assets tokenizer --hf_token=... MODULE=torchtitan_recipes.models.llama3 CONFIG=llama3_8b ./run_train.sh # 8 GPUs 4. Make it yours. A recipe is a Python function returning a complete config, so changing a run means writing a function, not passing flags: # my_recipes.py from torchtitan_recipes.models.llama3 import llama3_8b def llama3_8b_tp2(): config = llama3_8b() config.parallelism.tensor_parallel_degree = 2 return config MODULE=my_recipes CONFIG=llama3_8b_tp2 ./run_train.sh See the configuration guide for the full model, and torchtitan_recipes for the verified recipes. Supported models Model Sizes Modality Verified recipes RL Llama 3 1B – 405B Text llama3_8b, llama3_70b ✅ Qwen3 0.6B – 32B dense; 30B-A3B, 235B-A22B MoE Text qwen3_14b ✅ Qwen3.5 / 3.6 / 3.8 0.8B – 397B-A17B; 2.4T-A95B (3.8) Text, vision ✅ text DeepSeek V3 16B, 236B, 671B Text deepseek_v3_671b (+ Dist-MoE, NVFP4) DeepSeek V4 Flash, Pro Text Soon gpt-oss 20B, 120B Text ✅ Kimi K2.7 Moonlight-16B-A3B, Kimi-VL-A3B, K2.5 Text, vision Kimi K3 K3 Text, vision Soon Muse Glimmer 30B Text, vision muse_glimmer_30b ✅ Muse-Spark-Open 816B-A42B Text, vision, audio muse_spark_816b_a42b_dist_moe_bf16_spmd_256 ✅ text FLUX dev, schnell Text-to-image flux_dev, flux_schnell Every model has debug configurations exercised in CI. Verified recipes have been run in training, convergence, or performance workflows. To add a model, see the model guide. Features Parallelism FSDP2, HSDP, and DDP Tensor parallel, including async TP Pipeline parallel: 1F1B, Interleaved 1F1B, GPipe, and other torch.distributed.pipelining schedules Context parallel: all-gather KV and Ulysses Expert parallel with DeepEP / HybridEP dispatch Dist-MoE: fused dispatch, expert compute, and combine on Blackwell Memory and performance Activation checkpointing: full, selective, and regional Activation offloading to CPU of the activations remat (activation checkpointing) retains Regional torch.compile and CUDA graphs MXFP8 and NVFP4 training FlashAttention 3/4, FlexAttention, and varlen attention BF16 optimizer states and FSDP CPU offload Training Grain data pipeline with packing, mixing, and checkpointable state Pretraining, SFT on chat datasets, and LoRA Muon (DistMuon), EMA, multi-token prediction Warmup-stable-decay LR schedule and validation Post-training with TitanRL One model definition shared by the trainer and vLLM Bitwise trainer/generator parity in batch-invariant mode Async rollouts orchestrated with Monarch; trainer-to-generator model state dict transfer over TorchStore GRPO and DAPO losses; DAPO Math, Search-R1, and Verifiers examples Checkpointing Distributed checkpointing, including async saves Load and save Hugging Face safetensors directly Conversion scripts between HF and DCP Debugging and observability Metrics: loss, memory, throughput, TFLOPs, and MFU in TensorBoard or W&B Profiling and memory snapshots Flight Recorder and other debugging tools Fake-backend dry runs of large layouts on one GPU Deterministic mode and loss comparison across commits SDC replay and structured logging Extensibility Python recipes selected with --module and --config Component overrides for custom kernels and modules Experiments: GraphTrainer, TorchFT, Transformers modeling backend We report performance on up to 512 GPUs and verify loss convergence across parallelisms and techniques. Test status Hardware Integration tests Unit tests CPU NVIDIA GPU AMD GPU (ROCm) RL (NVIDIA GPU) Installation The quick start installs from source, which is the recommended way to get the latest features. Other options: Nightly builds pip install --pre torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/nightly/cu132 --force-reinstall pip install --pre torchtitan --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/nightly/cu132 Replace cu132 with another CUDA version or a ROCm build (e.g. rocm10.0). Stable releases pip install torchtitan # or conda install conda-forge::torchtitan Each stable release pins the nightly versions of torch and torchao it was validated against; see RELEASE.md. Optional dependencies Low precision (MXFP8, NVFP4): install the torchao nightly CI pins, from the index matching your torch build. It is not in requirements.txt so it cannot be resolved against a different torch:USE_CPP=0 pip install --pre -r .github/requirements-torchao.txt --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/nightly/cu132 RL: scripts/install_rl_env.sh installs the vLLM, Monarch, and TorchStore nightlies and the FlashAttention build for your GPU. See the RL quick start. Extras for vision, FLUX, RL, and development are also available as pip install -e ".[vlm,flux,rl,dev]". Importing from elsewhere: the source tree runs as is; to import torchtitan from another directory, install it in editable mode without re-resolving dependencies: pip install -e . --no-deps. Multi-node training with Slurm Submit scripts/multinode_trainer.slurm with sbatch from the repository root. Set the node count in both the #SBATCH header and the torchrun --nnodes argument: #SBATCH --ntasks=2 #SBATCH --nodes=2 srun torchrun --nnodes 2 ... If a node does not have 8 GPUs, also adjust --nproc_per_node and #SBATCH --gpus-per-task. Documentation Topic Where Configuring runs and writing recipes torchtitan/config Adding a model torchtitan/models Parallelisms and distributed techniques torchtitan/distributed Datasets and data loading torchtitan/components/data Checkpointing and HF conversion torchtitan/components/checkpointer Reinforcement learning torchtitan/rl Debugging, reproducibility, and validating numerics docs/debugging.md Validation and evaluation docs/evaluation.md Benchmarks docs/benchmarks Tests and CI tests Contributing We look forward to your contributions! New ideas should start in the experiments folder; follow the experiments guidelines. For fixes and contributions to core, follow the contributing guidelines. Citation Our paper gives a detailed look at the parallelisms and optimizations in torchtitan, with advice on when to use each technique: TorchTitan: One-stop PyTorch native solution for production ready LLM pre-training. @inproceedings{ liang2025torchtitan, title={TorchTitan: One-stop PyTorch native solution for production ready {LLM} pretraining}, author={Wanchao Liang and Tianyu Liu and Less Wright and Will Constable and Andrew Gu and Chien-Chin Huang and Iris Zhang and Wei Feng and Howard Huang and Junjie Wang and Sanket Purandare and Gokul Nadathur and Stratos Idreos}, booktitle={The Thirteenth International Conference on Learning Representations}, year={2025}, url={https://openreview.net/forum?id=SFN6Wm7YBI} } License Source code is made available under a BSD 3 license.
